request: Read signed 8-bit integer from tag buffer at offset

candidates.prompt: One SQUARE flat software icon on pure white for READING a signed 8 bit integer. Show a large dark navy CRANE HOOK above a large orange rectangular block, visibly lifting it. On the block write exactly I8 in EXTRA LARGE BOLD WHITE SANS-SERIF text. Capital I MUST have broad horizontal bars at top and bottom, so it cannot look like digit 1. Make I8 occupy almost the whole block and stay legible at 30x18. No other text, no arrows, no shadows, no monitor, no hand. Keep artwork within middle 70 percent of square.

30x23.evidence: The I8 block and suspension remain visible.

29x29.evidence: I8 and suspended block remain distinct.

30x18.evidence: Barred I and both orange counters of 8 remain distinguishable; hook softens.

16x16.evidence: The small hook and letter details soften.

source.evidence: A navy hook lifts an orange block labeled I8 with barred I.

Below the spout hangs one large ORANGE ROUND DROPLET with white bold text I8 centered inside. The capital I has broad horizontal top and bottom bars, distinct from 1. I8 must be enormous and readable at 30x18. No other text, no arrows, no tag shape, no shadow. Use bold simplified shapes, central 70 percent of square.

candidates.prompt: One SQUARE flat software icon on white for retrieving a signed 8-bit value. A large dark navy circular BUFFER SOCKET sits lower left. An oversized ORANGE KEY-SHAPED VALUE TILE angles upward right as though being removed from the socket, with a broad rectangular head holding huge WHITE I8. Capital I has prominent horizontal top and bottom bars, never a digit 1. Keep the letters and silhouette clear at 30x18. No other text, no arrows, no shadow, no monitor. Artwork inside central 70 percent of square.

signature.composition: orange I8 key diagonally outside blue socket

29x29.evidence: I8 and key shape are visible.

30x18.correction: Use an unrotated and larger I8 label.
30x18.evidence: The angled I8 label is too small and softened to read reliably.

source.correction: Use a different extraction metaphor that does not resemble a key or lock.
source.evidence: The key inserted in a socket suggests unlocking rather than reading a typed buffer value and risks confusion with Unlock.vi.
